register.name: Reshumot / Sefer HaChukim (רשומות, ספר החוקים), published by the Government Printer; Knesset legislation database (main.knesset.gov.il) and Knesset Open Data (ParliamentInfo OData service) as official status references; consolidated Hebrew working text from 'The Open Book of Laws' (ספר החוקים הפתוח) on Hebrew Wikisource
register.access_notes: Israel has no free official consolidated register: the official text of each Act is its original Sefer HaChukim publication plus every amending Act. Verification for this round used two independent routes, roughly 45 requests in total, spaced about 2 seconds apart, with an honest self-identifying User-Agent ('canon-legislation-indexer/1.0 (legalese/canon research; contact michael.fairweather@gmail.com)'). (1) BLOCKED: the human-facing Knesset law pages at https://main.knesset.gov.il/Activity/Legislation/Laws/Pages/LawPrimary.aspx?lawitemid=<id> return a JavaScript bot challenge (a 589-byte stub containing a 'kramericaindustries.ac_v2.lib.js' / 'window.rbzns' Reblaze seed and an empty <body>); no attempt was made to work around it, and no law page was read there. (2) BLOCKED: https://www.gov.il/he/pages/reshumot returned HTTP 403 to a scripted request; not worked around. (3) WORKED: the Knesset's own Open Data OData service at https://knesset.gov.il/Odata/ParliamentInfo.svc/ returned HTTP 200 application/xml for its service document and JSON for every query. Every Act below was confirmed against the official KNS_IsraelLaw table (Hebrew name, KnessetNum, PublicationDate, LatestPublicationDate, LawValidityDesc) and against KNS_LawBinding (the 'החוק המקורי' binding row, which carries the original Sefer HaChukim page number, plus one 'מתקן' row per amending Act). Note KNS_Law and KNS_IsraelLawBinding do NOT cover these older enactments (both returned zero rows for the relevant LawIDs), so the Sefer HaChukim issue/booklet NUMBER could not be recovered from the official data for any of these Acts - only the Hebrew year and page number, which is how Israeli practice cites them anyway (e.g. 'ס"ח תשי"ח, 86'). (4) WORKED: https://he.wikisource.org/ returned HTTP 200 for every page fetched; one page per Act was read for the consolidated text and its printed ס"ח citation string, plus https://he.wikisource.org/wiki/ספר_החוקים_הפתוח (an A-to-T index page only; it carries no project disclaimer or updating statement in its fetched body) and https://he.wikisource.org/wiki/חוק_זכות_יוצרים for the licence position. (5) NOT AVAILABLE: no official Knesset English-language page for any of these Acts could be reached, because the Knesset site route is the bot-challenged one. The English titles below are therefore the conventional English renderings in common professional use, NOT verified against an official Knesset or Ministry of Justice English page - a human should confirm them before they are treated as the official English names.

licence.summary: Open. No copyright subsists in Israeli statutes: Copyright Act, 5768-2007 (חוק זכות יוצרים, התשס"ח-2007), s 6 excludes laws, regulations, Knesset proceedings and judicial decisions from copyright, notwithstanding s 4. There is therefore no licence to accept and no restriction on reproducing the statutory text itself. Separately, the Hebrew Wikisource transcription used as the consolidated working text is released by its contributors under CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia site-wide terms); that licence attaches to the Wikisource editors' consolidation work and formatting, not to the statutory text, which is uncopyrightable under s 6.
licence.attribution: No attribution is legally required for the statutory text (Copyright Act, 5768-2007, s 6). Where the consolidated Hebrew text is taken from Hebrew Wikisource, credit 'ספר החוקים הפתוח, ויקיטקסט העברי (CC BY-SA 4.0)' and state that it is an unofficial consolidation.
licence.quote: על אף הוראות סעיף 4, לא תהא זכות יוצרים בחוקים, בתקנות, בדברי הכנסת ובהחלטות שיפוטיות של בית משפט או של כל רשות שלטונית המפעילה סמכות שפיטה על פי דין.

il-employment.language_authenticity: Hebrew is authoritative; English translations are unofficial. The official text of each Act is the Hebrew text as published in Sefer HaChukim, as amended by every subsequent amending Act; the consolidated Hebrew Wikisource text is an unofficial (though maintained) consolidation and must never be presented as the official text.

acts.notes: Sets the statutory minimum wage as a proportion of the average wage and the monthly/daily/hourly derivations, with criminal and civil enforcement. The Knesset LatestPublicationDate (2017-11-07) and the Wikisource 'תשע"ח' last amendment are the same amendment cycle.

acts.title: Hours of Work and Rest Law, 5711-1951
acts.identifier: ס"ח תשי"א, 204 (Sefer HaChukim 5711, p 204); Knesset IsraelLawID 2000019; Wikisource page 'חוק שעות עבודה ומנוחה'
acts.verified_how: Knesset Open Data KNS_IsraelLaw record fetched 23 September 2026: IsraelLawID 2000019, Name 'חוק שעות עבודה ומנוחה, התשי"א-1951', KnessetNum 1, PublicationDate 1951-05-22, ValidityStartDate 1951-09-27, LatestPublicationDate 2018-06-21, LawValidityDesc 'תקף', ValidityFinishDate null, LastUpdatedDate 2025-09-15. KNS_LawBinding returned 19 rows: 1 'החוק המקורי' with PageNumber '204' and 18 'מתקן' rows. The Hebrew Wikisource page prints 'חוק שעות עבודה ומנוחה, תשי"א–1951', citation 'ס"ח תשי"א, 204' with amending years 5724 through 5778, and no repeal marker. A first read of the Wikisource page appeared to show a 5785/2025 change; a targeted re-read established that the two 5785-2025 items are general overtime permits issued UNDER the Law and published as notices - 'הודעה על מתן היתר כללי להעסקת עובדים בשעות נוספות (הוראת שעה), התשפ"ה–2025' and 'הודעה על מתן היתר כללי בדבר שעות נוספות והפסקות בתחבורה (הוראת שעה), התשפ"ה–2025' - not amendments to the statute. The official LatestPublicationDate of 2018-06-21 is therefore correct for statutory amendments, and there is no discrepancy between the two sources.
acts.notes: TOPIC ALLOCATION (asked for explicitly): filed under Payroll/wages, not Leave/holiday pay. Reason: the Law's operative money rules are payroll computation rules - it caps the ordinary working day and week and then fixes the PREMIUM RATES payable for overtime and for work on the weekly rest, so in practice it is the statute that determines what a lawful payslip must pay for hours worked. Its weekly-rest and rest-break provisions are about mandatory non-working hours within a working week, which is a different thing from paid annual or holiday leave; Israel puts paid leave entitlement in the Annual Leave Law and the Sick Pay Law, which are filed under Leave/holiday pay. A human who prefers a 'working time' topic should note this Act would be its natural anchor. Also note that a large part of the practical regime sits in general permits (היתר כללי) issued under the Law rather than in the Law itself - see verified_how - so an encoding of the statute alone will not reproduce the sectoral overtime rules.

acts.title: Women's Employment Law, 5714-1954
acts.identifier: ס"ח תשי"ד, 154 (Sefer HaChukim 5714, p 154); Knesset IsraelLawID 2001135; Wikisource page 'חוק עבודת נשים'
acts.verified_how: Knesset Open Data KNS_IsraelLaw record fetched 23 September 2026: IsraelLawID 2001135, Name 'חוק עבודת נשים, התשי"ד-1954', KnessetNum 2, PublicationDate 1954-08-12, ValidityStartDate 1954-08-12, LatestPublicationDate 2026-03-31, LawValidityDesc 'תקף', ValidityFinishDate null, LastUpdatedDate 2025-09-15. KNS_LawBinding returned 73 rows: 1 'החוק המקורי' with PageNumber '154' and 72 'מתקן' rows - the most heavily amended Act in this group. The Hebrew Wikisource page 'חוק עבודת נשים' prints 'חוק עבודת נשים, תשי"ד–1954', citation 'ס"ח תשי"ד, 154' with amendments through 'תשפ"ו, 563', page last edited 1 June 2026, and no repeal marker for the Act itself. The Wikisource text records that this Act repealed (בוטל, in its s 25) the Mandate-era Women's Employment Ordinance 1945 (פקודת העבדתן של נשים), confirming that the 1954 Knesset Law and not the Ordinance is the operative instrument. Wikisource also flags a temporary provision (הוראת שעה) in s 9(c)(2c) running 31 March 2026 to 31 March 2027, which matches the official LatestPublicationDate of 2026-03-31.
acts.notes: This is the maternity/parental leave statute (חופשת לידה / תקופת לידה והורות): length of leave, the right to extend or shorten it, leave for the other parent, nursing-hour deductions from the working day, and the prohibition on dismissal during and after the leave. TWO things a human must check. (1) A temporary provision in s 9(c)(2c) is in force only from 31 March 2026 to 31 March 2027 - an encoding must carry that sunset. (2) This Act confers the RIGHT to leave; the maternity/parental ALLOWANCE that makes the leave paid (דמי לידה) is paid by the National Insurance Institute under the National Insurance Law [Consolidated Version], 5755-1995, which is not indexed here. Encoding this Act alone gives leave entitlement and dismissal protection, not the money. Note also that the dismissal-protection provisions straddle this topic and Termination/severance.

Pairs with the Entry into Israel Law below: this Act governs the employer and the employment relationship, the Entry Law governs the worker's visa.

acts.notes: The general visa and residence-permit statute, and the instrument under which a work visa (B/1) is actually issued: categories of visa and permit, powers of the Minister of the Interior and border-control officers, conditions, extension, revocation, removal and custody. THREE cautions. (1) Much of the operative detail is in subordinate legislation - the Entry into Israel Regulations, 5734-1974 and annual quota orders (צווי מכסה שנתית) - so the Act alone does not state the visa classes' conditions in full. (2) Some provisions are subject to sunset clauses (Wikisource flags one running to 24 April 2027); an encoding must carry them. (3) Do NOT confuse this Act with the Citizenship and Entry into Israel (Temporary Provision) Laws of 2003 and 2022, which are separate, narrower and time-limited instruments - see verified_how for their official status.

topic_gaps.reason: PARTIAL gap, for the 'holiday pay' component only. The two paid-leave statutes above (Annual Leave Law 5711-1951 and Sick Pay Law 5736-1976) plus the Women's Employment Law 5714-1954 for maternity/parental leave cover the topic's statutory core. But pay for public and religious holidays (דמי חגים) is NOT conferred by any Knesset statute: in Israel it comes from general collective-agreement extension orders (צווי הרחבה) made under the Collective Agreements Law, and from individual collective agreements, with the Hours of Work and Rest Law 5711-1951 supplying only the premium rate for work actually performed on a holiday or the weekly rest. Separately, the MONEY that makes maternity/parental leave paid is a National Insurance benefit (דמי לידה) under the National Insurance Law [Consolidated Version], 5755-1995, which belongs to a social-security topic rather than this one. A complete 'holiday pay' encoding for Israel therefore needs extension orders, which are not statutes and are not in this index.

PARTIAL gap, noted for completeness rather than as a missing statute. The three Acts above are the operative statutory core (payment mechanics and delayed-wage compensation; the minimum-wage formula; overtime and rest-day premium rates). Two things a payroll encoding still needs and will not find in them: (a) the current shekel minimum-wage figure, which is set by the updating mechanism together with extension orders and Ministry of Labour notices rather than printed in the Minimum Wage Law; and (b) payroll tax and social-insurance withholding, which sit in the Income Tax Ordinance [New Version], 5721-1961 and the National Insurance Law [Consolidated Version], 5755-1995 - both outside this group's four topics.

PARTIAL gap. The two Acts above are the correct operative statutes (employer duties and permit offences; visas and residence permits). But the conditions attaching to each visa class, and the annual sectoral quotas for foreign workers, are set by subordinate legislation under the Entry into Israel Law - principally the Entry into Israel Regulations, 5734-1974 and the annual quota orders (צווי הכניסה לישראל (מכסה שנתית)) - and by Population and Immigration Authority procedures (נוהלים), none of which are statutes. Anyone encoding work-permit eligibility as opposed to work-permit offences will be working mostly outside the statute book.
